summary: Letter, pass 3 is a foundation fix followed by structure, then behaviour. The code at HEAD contradicts what pass 2 was described as: src/constants/chat-surfaces.ts holds translucent rgba surfaces (0.74 to 0.9), so everything built on top of them (a 1px white hairline on every filled bubble, a 4px text shadow on every 9 to 12px label, greys tuned for pure black) was added to fight the photo instead of standing on a solid ground. Items 1 to 4 fix that ground: solid tokens, one edge device per surface (fill only for content, the artist's silver line as the only line, a hairline only on controls), no text shadows, day and time separators on solid chips with AM/PM, and no loose clocks on the runs. Items 5 to 10 fix structure to Instagram and iMessage geometry: a real composer bar down to the home indicator with a mic-to-send swap, grouped bubble corners with the avatar on the last bubble, a truly centred fixed-height header seeded from the list row, one 16px gutter, a grouped list panel with real unread emphasis, and a top fade that no longer dims the first row. Items 11 to 23 make the thread behave: optimistic send with a failed state, scroll-to-latest and a new-messages chip, an anchored long-press toolbar shared with the post screen, one notice pill component, aspect-fit media with a viewer, Seen and Sent in the DM, contrast, Anton discipline, motion and haptics, a real voice pill, a real recording state, a solid loading skeleton, and tappable links. Left out on purpose (features, not polish, for a separate yes from the owner): typing indicator and presence, swipe actions on list rows, rolling the 28px letterhead out to the other four tabs.
root_causes: The bubbles, cards and composer were quietly made see-through again (chat-surfaces.ts is rgba 0.74 to 0.9), so shadows, outlines and dim greys were piled on top to fight the photo instead of sitting on a solid surface you already asked for three times.
Every surface has both a fill and an outline. That is the 'outlined card' look of a first app; Instagram and iMessage use one or the other, never both.

Small text (times, names, day labels) sits loose on the photo with a blur shadow and greys that were picked for pure black, not charcoal. The apps you benchmark never put loose 11px text over a wallpaper: they put it on a chip, inside the bubble, or behind a tap.

The screens copied the mockup's pixels but not its structure: four different side gutters, a header that is 15px off centre and jumps after load, bubbles in a run that are not grouped, an avatar aligned to nothing, and a composer floating with no bar under it or under the home indicator.

Nothing responds. Messages wait for the server before they appear, the thread does not scroll when you send, nothing animates or buzzes, the moderation bar shoves the whole conversation up, and there is no Seen, no new-message pill, no optimistic anything. Static polish reads as rookie no matter how the pixels are tuned.

spec.change: Make every chat surface solid and define one neutral scale in one file. This is the ground everything else in the pass stands on; nothing below works over translucent fills.

Replace the bare day label and the per-run clocks with the Instagram/iMessage scheme: a small centred solid chip that shows day and time whenever the day changes or more than an hour passes, and no loose clock on any run (tap a bubble to see its time). This removes all bare small text from the photo except the sender name.
